text: Reviews pull requests automatically within moments of opening, using multiple AI models to post actionable feedback
quote: Within moments of opening a pull request, CodeRabbit analyzes your code with multiple AI models and provides actionable feedback, catching issues that are easy to miss in manual reviews.

text: Signs up and connects through existing GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket Cloud, or Bitbucket Data Center accounts
quote: Use your existing GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket Cloud, or Bitbucket Data Center account to create your CodeRabbit account. No credit card required!

text: Detects runtime errors, null pointer exceptions, race conditions, and logic flaws before deployment
quote: Spot potential runtime errors, null pointer exceptions, race conditions, and logic flaws before deployment

text: Runs AI code reviews from the CLI before commit, catching race conditions, memory leaks, and security vulnerabilities
quote: Get AI code reviews directly in your CLI before you commit. Catch race conditions, memory leaks, and security vulnerabilities without leaving your development environment.

text: Runs reviews in CI/CD pipelines as well as on uncommitted local changes
quote: Review uncommitted changes as you code, apply fixes instantly, integrate seamlessly with your AI coding agents, or run reviews in CI/CD pipelines.

text: Gives review feedback inside VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other VS Code-based IDEs
quote: Get instant feedback in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and any VS Code-based IDE.

text: Reviews uncommitted changes in the development environment without a pull request and applies fixes instantly
quote: CodeRabbit brings AI-powered code reviews directly into your development environment, no pull request required. Review uncommitted changes as you code, apply fixes instantly

text: AI Deep Scan analyzes committed code and infrastructure config beyond the PR diff for exploitable vulnerabilities and exposed secrets
quote: AI Deep Scan is a separately metered scan that analyzes committed source code and infrastructure configuration for exploitable vulnerabilities and exposed secrets beyond the current pull request diff.

text: Supports linters and SAST tools as part of reviews
quote: Linters and SAST tools support

text: Users can ask follow-up questions, request clarifications, challenge recommendations, or explore alternatives in conversation
quote: you can ask follow-up questions, request clarifications, challenge recommendations, or explore alternative approaches

text: Learns review preferences from chat conversations and applies them automatically to future reviews
quote: Review preferences CodeRabbit learns from your chat conversations and applies automatically to future reviews.

text: Applies path-specific review instructions using glob patterns, e.g. security checks for controllers and coverage rules for tests
quote: Path instructions apply targeted guidance to specific paths, such as security checks for API controllers, coverage requirements for tests, or clarity rules for documentation.

text: Supports syntax-aware review rules based on AST patterns powered by ast-grep
quote: CodeRabbit supports review instructions based on Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) patterns, powered by ast-grep

text: Automatically detects guideline files such as .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md and applies them as review criteria
quote: CodeRabbit automatically detects coding guideline files such as .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md in your repository and applies them as review criteria

text: Path filters exclude files such as lock files, binaries, and generated code from review
quote: Path filters exclude files that don't benefit from review: lock files, binaries, and generated code.

text: Linked repositories let reviews detect breaking changes, API mismatches, and dependency issues across repo boundaries
quote: Link related repositories so CodeRabbit can detect breaking changes, API mismatches, and dependency issues that cross repository boundaries during code review.

text: Uses MCP servers as knowledge sources for context from docs, design tools, and project management during reviews and chat
quote: Use MCP servers as a knowledge source to give CodeRabbit additional context from your documentation systems, design tools, and project management platforms during reviews and chat.

text: One-click agentic actions fix review findings, resolve merge conflicts, generate unit tests, simplify code, and run custom recipes
quote: One-click agentic actions that polish and extend your pull requests or merge requests: fix review findings, resolve merge conflicts, generate unit tests, simplify code, run any custom recipes.

text: Generates the code changes needed to fix identified issues, not just flags them
quote: One of CodeRabbit's powerful features is its ability to not just identify issues, but also generate the code changes needed to fix them.

text: Applies suggested changes directly to the PR with a single click
quote: Apply suggested changes directly to your PR with a single click—no copy-paste, no switching contexts

text: Can be prompted to generate its own improvements to the pull request
quote: Prompt CodeRabbit to generate its own improvements to the pull request

text: Org-wide configuration is maintained in a dedicated coderabbit repository holding a shared .coderabbit.yaml
quote: Maintain CodeRabbit configuration for your entire organization in one dedicated repository. Create a `coderabbit` repository in your organization and add your `.coderabbit.yaml` file

text: Review command does an incremental review of new changes; a full-review command re-reviews the entire PR
quote: @coderabbitai review does incremental review (new changes), not a full review. Use @coderabbitai full review when you want a complete pass over the entire pull request.

text: Review triggers are configurable: disable globally, re-enable by keyword or label, filter by branch, skip drafts, pause after N commits
quote: you can disable reviews globally and re-enable them by keyword or label, apply them only to certain branches, skip draft PRs, and pause after a set number of commits

text: @coderabbitai commands pause, resume, or ignore reviews, request manual reviews, resolve comments, request approval, and update summaries
quote: Pause, resume, ignore reviews, request manual reviews, resolve comments, request approval, and update pull request summaries using @coderabbitai commands.

text: Command reference includes commands for generating documentation and managing pull requests
quote: Complete reference of CodeRabbit commands for controlling code reviews, generating documentation, and managing pull requests.

text: @coderabbitai configuration command returns the resolved configuration in YAML on any PR
quote: Use the `@coderabbitai configuration` command on any PR to get the resolved configuration in YAML format.

text: Claude Code can trigger CodeRabbit reviews via commands to build, review, and fix issues without manual intervention
quote: Claude Code can trigger CodeRabbit reviews directly through simple commands, enabling you to build features, run code reviews, and fix issues without manual intervention.

text: Agentic code reviews run inside loops with coding agents as well as in PR, CLI, and IDE
quote: Agentic code reviews in PR, CLI, IDE, and in agent loops

text: Turns ideas, issues, PRDs, and designs into codebase-grounded Coding Plans to hand off to any coding agent
quote: Turn ideas, issues, PRDs, and designs into precise Coding Plans grounded in your codebase, then hand them off to any coding agent.

text: Self-hosted option runs the review agent inside the customer's own infrastructure
quote: Self-hosted CodeRabbit runs the CodeRabbit review agent inside your own infrastructure instead of CodeRabbit's cloud.

text: Customer code is never used for model training by CodeRabbit, OpenAI, or Anthropic
quote: FAQ, data privacy: "Your proprietary code remains confidential with CodeRabbit. CodeRabbit never uses customer code for model training." and "Neither CodeRabbit, OpenAI, nor Anthropic uses your code to train our models."

text: Data retention is controllable, with full opt-out on self-hosted Enterprise and a separate setting for model output logging
quote: FAQ, data retention controls: "Data retention only affects storage of code-related data such as learnings and review context"; "On self-hosted CodeRabbit (available for Enterprise), you can opt out of all data retention at any time"; model

text: Dashboard tracks review speed, code quality, collaboration patterns, bottlenecks, and ROI of AI reviews across the org
quote: Dashboard guide: "The CodeRabbit Dashboard provides visibility into your team's review speed, code quality, collaboration patterns, and the impact of AI-assisted reviews. Use the dashboard to track performance, identify bottlenecks, and mea

text: Request Changes Workflow blocks PRs with actionable comments and approves once requirements and Pre-Merge Checks are met
quote: Request changes workflow: "Request Changes Workflow keeps CodeRabbit's review decision synchronized with its actionable feedback. When enabled, CodeRabbit requests changes when a review posts actionable inline comments and approves the pull

text: Investigate feature answers natural-language codebase questions and cross-references Sentry errors with merged PRs and Jira issues
quote: Investigate — Ask questions about your codebase, trace features, and cross-reference Sentry errors with merged PRs and Jira issues, all in natural language.

text: Slack integration brings AI investigation, planning, and code editing with shared context and governed access
quote: Bring AI-powered investigation, planning, and code editing into your Slack workspace: with shared context, persistent knowledge, and governed access.

text: Triage provides a self-updating cross-repository PR queue prioritized by value and risk
quote: Triage — a self-updating cross-repository queue that prioritizes pull requests by value and risk, so you always know what to review next.

text: Surfaces changes needing attention and routes each pull request to the right reviewer
quote: Prioritize your PR queue by value and risk, surface the changes that need attention, and route each pull request to the right reviewer.

text: Users can override Triage ranking when they know something CodeRabbit does not
quote: how to override the ranking when you know something CodeRabbit does not

text: Triage queue offers views, search, filters, grouping, layouts, saved and team views, and Focus lanes
quote: Cut a large queue down to the pull requests that are actually yours — with built-in views, search, filters, grouping, two layouts, saved views, team views, and Focus lanes.

text: PRs can be reviewed, repaired, reassigned, merged, closed, and followed directly from the Triage queue
quote: Review, repair, reassign, merge, close, and follow a pull request from the Triage queue

text: Delivers the Triage queue as a scheduled Slack digest, sends reviewer requests, and approves or closes PRs from Slack
quote: Get your Triage queue as a scheduled digest, send reviewer requests to the people who should act on them, and approve or close a pull request without leaving Slack.

text: Integrates with Jira and Linear
quote: Jira and Linear integrations

text: Appends a generated summary to the PR description grouping changes by type
quote: CodeRabbit appends a generated summary to the bottom of the PR description after a review. The summary groups changes by type

text: Posts a structured walkthrough comment at the top of the PR thread on every review
quote: Every time CodeRabbit reviews a pull request, it posts a **walkthrough comment** — a structured overview of the changes that appears at the top of the PR comment thread

text: Breaks large diffs into logical cohorts and layers with range-specific summaries and diagrams
quote: Understand large diffs as logical cohorts and layers, with range-specific summaries and diagrams that show how each change fits together.

text: Reads CI/CD failure output and posts inline comments with suggested fixes on the lines that caused the failure
quote: When a CI/CD pipeline fails on a pull request, CodeRabbit reads the failure output and posts inline comments with suggested fixes — directly on the lines of code that caused the failure.

text: Assesses linked issues to check whether a pull request actually addresses their requirements
quote: CodeRabbit provides intelligent assessment of linked issues to validate whether pull requests properly address their requirements.

text: Automatically detects low-quality AI-generated slop pull requests on GitHub
quote: Automatically detect low-quality, AI-generated 'Slop' pull requests on GitHub repositories.

text: Change Stack turns a PR into a structured, navigable review workspace you can read, question, and act on
quote: Change Stack is CodeRabbit's review workspace: it turns a pull request into a structured, navigable artifact you can read, question, and act on in one place.

text: Users can ask questions about a change in a conversation pinned to its review snapshot
quote: Ask questions about the change you are reviewing in a conversation pinned to its review snapshot.

text: Change Stack supports search, tracking what has been read, and shareable deep links
quote: search the artifact, track what you have already read, and share a link that points where you mean.

text: Change Stack presents code, prose, and image diffs with controls to bring in more context
quote: How Change Stack presents code, prose, and image diffs, and the controls that bring more context into view.

text: Shows findings for a change, judges merge readiness, and helps decide what to fix first
quote: Read what CodeRabbit found in a change, judge how ready it is to merge, and decide what to fix first.

text: Users can write and submit reviews, apply suggestions, and merge or enqueue PRs from inside Change Stack
quote: Write and submit a review, apply suggestions, and merge or enqueue a pull request from inside Change Stack.

text: Carries a Change Stack review into Slack or Discord threads and subscribes PRs to events
quote: Carry a Change Stack review into a Slack or Discord thread, subscribe the pull request to events, and choose how fixes land.
